meta.title: Kings League, Explained: The Football League Built Like a Video Game
meta.description: How Gerard Piqué's 7-a-side Kings League works: the Scale-Up, secret cards, the dice, Matchball Mode, the streamer presidents and why millions watch. Interactive guide.
meta.ogDescription: Secret cards, a giant dice and streamer presidents. An interactive guide to the football league built like a video game.

ui.pitchAlt: Illustration of a seven-a-side pitch with seven players on each team

hero.title: Kings League, Explained: The Football League Built Like a Video Game
hero.subtitle: Seven a side, 36 minutes, secret cards and a giant dice. How it works, and why millions tune in.

paragraphs: Picture a Tuesday night five-a-side game, then hand the rulebook to a room full of streamers. That's more or less the Kings League. Gerard Piqué, the former Barcelona and Spain defender, presented it on 10 November 2022: seven against seven, short halves, and rules that sound like they came out of a video game menu. Coaches hold secret cards. A giant dice decides how many players stay on the pitch. Team presidents can walk down from the stands and take a penalty.

It works because it lives where people already watch. Every match streams free on Twitch, YouTube and TikTok, and on the channels of presidents who bring their own millions of followers. In the first season in Spain, a single matchday-three game passed 1.3 million viewers. I'm Colombian and I come from five-a-side football (I'm building a booking platform for small-sided games in Bogotá), so I paid close attention when Colombia made the final of the Kings World Cup Nations in January 2025. We lost 6–2 to Brazil in Turin. Still, a final.

timeline.title: Anatomy of a match
timeline.lead: A Kings League game is a sequence of short phases, each with its own rule. Tap or hover a phase to see what happens.

segments.title: Scale-Up: from 1v1 to 7v7
segments.body: It starts 1v1 plus keepers: the ball drops from a cage and both players sprint for it. Every minute each side adds a player: 2v2, 3v3, and so on until it's 7v7 at minute 5.

segments.title: First card window
segments.body: Coaches can press the green button to play their secret card. A president who is in the stadium can press the blue one for a President Penalty.

segments.title: Double goals
segments.body: A ball of a different colour comes on and every goal counts double until half-time. There's no added time, so the last seconds before the break get chaotic.

segments.title: Half-time and the dice
segments.body: The second half opens with a roll of a giant dice. Logo means 1v1, a 2 means 2v2, a 3 means 3v3, always plus keepers. By minute 23 everyone is back on.

segments.title: Second card window
segments.body: Secret cards and President Penalties are live again. Teams that saved their card for a tight finish use it here.

segments.title: Matchball Mode or shootouts
segments.body: Level at 36? Straight to shootouts. Someone ahead? Matchball Mode: if the leader scores, it's over. If the trailing team equalises, the next goal wins. Meanwhile it's a Scale-Down, from 5v5 losing one player a side every minute down to 1v1.

cards.title: The secret cards
cards.lead: Before kick-off each coach draws one card at random. Nobody knows what the other bench is holding. Tap a card to flip it.
cards.label: Secret card

items.name: Goal x2
items.body: Every goal your team scores counts double for the next four minutes.

items.name: Suspension
items.body: Pick a rival (any player except the keeper). They sit out for four minutes.

items.name: Star Player
items.body: Choose one player. Their first goal counts double. They wear an armband so everyone knows who it is.

items.name: Shootout
items.body: Ball on the centre spot. One of your players gets five seconds to beat the keeper one on one.

items.name: Joker
items.body: Play it as any of the other cards, or steal the card your rival is holding.

items.name: Reverse Penalty
items.body: Fans voted it in for 2025/26. You pick a rival to take a penalty. If they score, it doesn't count. If they miss, the goal is yours.

items.name: Penalty
items.body: A traditional penalty kick. The most normal thing in the deck.

dice.title: Roll the dice
dice.lead: The second half starts with a giant dice. It has three faces, each printed twice: a logo, a 2 and a 3. Whatever lands decides how many outfield players each team keeps for three minutes.
dice.prompt: Press Roll to start the second half.

logo.label: 1v1
logo.text: Logo: one outfield player each, plus keepers. Acres of space.

2.label: 2v2
2.text: Two each, plus keepers. Give-and-go football.

3.label: 3v3
3.text: Three each, plus keepers. The closest thing to a street game.

dice.odds: Each result has the same chance: 2 in 6.
dice.logoNote: The logo on this dice is a generic badge made for this page, not the league's.

expansion.title: From Barcelona to the world
expansion.lead: In four years the format went from one league in Spain to seven regions and two World Cups. A US league was announced in June 2025; as of November 2026 it isn't on the official list yet.

quote.text: The rulebook works like patch notes. Fans vote, presidents argue, and next season plays by the result.
quote.author: Johan Torres

paragraphs.heading: Built for clips
paragraphs.text: A normal match asks for two hours of your attention. A Kings League game gives you a reason to look up every few minutes: the Scale-Up, a secret card, double goals, the dice, Matchball. Each one is a ready-made clip. That suits the way a lot of Gen Z follows sport, in short pieces on a phone, on TikTok and YouTube as much as on a TV. You can catch the last five minutes and still feel you saw the whole story.

paragraphs.heading: Presidents are the distribution
paragraphs.text: The presidents are the marketing. When Ibai or Gaules streams a match, the game lands on a channel whose audience was already there. The league doesn't have to build a fan base from zero in every country; it borrows one and turns it into a rivalry. It's also how the format travels. Italy, Brazil, France, Germany and MENA each got their own local creators and ex-players as presidents, not imports from Spain.

paragraphs.heading: Fans hold the controller
paragraphs.text: Then there's the vote. Fans have shaped the rules from the start, and the newest card, Reverse Penalty, won a public vote for 2025/26. That turns viewers into stakeholders. Like a patch in a video game, the rules shift between seasons and people tune in to see how the new meta plays out. Which is also why this guide has a date on it.

questions.q: How long is the first half?
questions.explain: The first half is 20 minutes and the second is 16, then Matchball Mode or shootouts.

questions.q: Between which minutes do all goals count double?
questions.explain: From minute 17 to half-time a different-coloured ball comes on and every goal counts double.

questions.q: The giant dice lands on the logo. What happens?
questions.explain: Logo means 1v1 plus keepers. A 2 means 2v2 and a 3 means 3v3.

questions.q: You play Reverse Penalty and your rival misses the kick. What happens?
questions.explain: With Reverse Penalty, a goal by the rival doesn't count, and a miss gives the goal to the team that played the card.

questions.q: It's level at minute 36. What comes next?
questions.explain: A tie at 36 goes straight to shootouts. Matchball Mode only happens when one team is ahead.
